Name: 3_woman_piece_tomorrow_cut
Representative_Docs:
["1.  
Happy New Year!  
Pull the cat by the hair,  
Pull the dog at the start,  
Then you have something all year round.  

2.  
Good luck in the new year!  
Father and mother sleep together,  
And I sleep in the cradle.  
May I have a little ear (of grain)?  

3.  
I wish you much luck and blessing,  
On dikes and roads,  
With curls in your hair.  
I wish you luck and blessing in the new year.  

4.  
Day woman, day man, day everyone  
I come to wish you a happy new year.  
Through thick and thin, I come walking;  
Don't you have a waffle or two? I will not sell them.  
It's a good woman who gives something;  
I wish she lives the coming year as well.  
Good woman! Good woman!  
Don't you have a waffle or two? I will already put them in my sleeve.  

5.  
It is New Year, I stand here outside  
I have a little basket, and it won't close;  
I have a little knife, and it won't cut;  
I have butter, but it won't fry;  
I see a cookie and cannot buy it;  
Give me a penny, and let me go.  

6.  
New Year comes to the land;  
The pig has burned its tail,  
From behind its little gate.  
Mother, give me a little ear;  
If it's not an ear, then it's a penny,  
Tomorrow New Year will be over.  

7.  
Sweet little New Year,  
The pig has four feet,  
Four feet and one tail,  
Isn’t that worth a cookie?  
It hasn’t stood long in the stable,  
Janneef has killed it,  
Give me a cookie and let me go.  

2.  
Palm-, palm-Easter;  
A little rooster on a stick,  
A hole through its jacket,  
A piece of its left foot;  
Now the whole little rooster is dead.  

3.  
Palm-, palm-Easter, hey, cow song;  
It still takes one Sunday,  
Then we go to the Easter meadow.  

4.  
Palm-, palm-Sunday,  
When the farmer was in the water,  
I was there, and you were there,  
Wasn’t that a beautiful picture?  
Woman, woman give us an egg,  
That the black hens laid,  
Do they see black or are they red?  
That's why they don't lay too badly.  
A, B, C, D. give us a clerk,  
Bake us a pancake,  
Give us eggs and enough money.  
Woman, woman at last,  
Give us the laid eggs,  
Laid and well liked,  
Let us stay a little longer.

How long will she live!  
The first year a penny,  
The second year a shilling,  
The third year a pound of cookies,  
Give us eggs and enough money.  
Reach a little deeper into the nest,  
The black hens lay best,  
The red hens not less,  
Reach a little deeper again,  
Master and wife stay healthy.
